text: The PI and his collaborators have also used the isospin-dependent relativistic Vlasov- Uehling-Uhlenbeck (RVUU) model, which he developed in 1980s, to study charged pion √ production in Au+Au collisions at s = 2.4 GeV measured by the HADES Collabo- NN ration at GSI [3] and found that to describe the measured pion rapidity distributions and transverse momentum spectra in various collision centralities requires a density-dependent Delta resonance production cross section that is smaller than its value measured in free space. 2 2) Light nuclei production in heavy ion collisions. The PI and his collaborators have developed a kinetic approach to the production of light nuclei, such as deuteron, triton, helium-3 and the alpha particle, in heavy ion collisions by including them in the transport model as dynamic degrees of freedom with their production and destruction described by nucleon and pion catalyzed multi-nucleon reactions and their reverse reactions. They have found that the measured yields of light nuclei in central Au + Au collisions at energies of 0.25A GeV - 1.0A GeV by the FOPI Collaboration can be well described after including their Mott effects due to the Pauli blocking of their internal momentum states on their binding energies [4]. An unexpectedly abundant alpha clustering was found in the warm and dense matter produced in these collisions [5], which will have profound implications for modeling the nuclear equation of state and describing supernovae and neutron star mergers. For relativistic heavy heavy ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC, assuming light nuclei are initially produced statistically from the hadronization hypersurface of the viscous hydrodynamic model MUSIC with a crossover type of equation of state, the pion catalyzed multi-nucleon reactions was found to have little effects on the deuteron yield but reduce the triton and helium-3 yields by about a factor of 1.8 from their initial values [6], which is in excellent agreement with the latest experimental data and thus provides the evidence for the importance of hadronic re-scattering effects on the little bang nucleosynthesis in relativistic √ heavy-ion collisions. In pp collisions at s = 13 TeV, the pion-catalyzed production of NN light nuclei was shown to give rise to a pion-deuteron femtoscopic correlation that peaks near the Delta resonance mass [7] as observed in the ALICE experiments. Based on an extended Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with an eight-quark scalar-vector in- teractiontoallowthecriticalpointtohaveaflexiblelocationintheQCDphasediagram, the PI and his collaborators have studied the effect of a first-order phase transition on the yield ratio N N /N2 of produced proton (p), deuteron (d), and triton (t). It was found that the t p d large density fluctuations generated by the spinodal instability during the first-order phase transition could survive the subsequent fast expansion of the hadronic matter and lead to an √ enhanced yield ratio N N /N2 in central collisions at s = 3−5 GeV [8, 9]. Discussions t p d NN on the potential use of the yield ratio N N /N2 to search for the QCD critical point was t p d published by the PI as a research highlight paper in Nuclear Science and Technique [10].
